blocks.text: This page tracks the Langley MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $932,900 for a typical home, down 5.7% over twelve months.
Langley benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Langley home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $932,900 in October 2026. That is little changed at −1.0% on the month, down 2.4% over three months, down 3.9% over six months and down 5.7% over the year. Over three years it is down 10.4%, and over five years down 4.9%.
The weakest one-year move in Langley was for an apartment homes at −8.4%; the strongest was a townhouse at −3.7%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,448,100) and an apartment ($522,300) is $925,800, and a townhouse ($800,600) sits $278,300 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $860,000, Langley is 8.5% above. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 6.4% against down 5.7% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, Langley ranks 3 by all-home benchmark, with South Surrey & White Rock above it at $996,000 and Cloverdale below it at $930,600.

Detached homes in Langley: benchmark $1,448,100, down 1.6% in a month, down 3.5% in three months, down 5.1% in six months, down 6.5% in a year, down 10.8% in three years and down 7.2% in five. That is 11.9% above the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,293,800).

Townhouse homes in Langley: benchmark $800,600, little changed at −0.2% in a month, little changed at −1.3% in three months, little changed at −1.4% in six months, down 3.7% in a year, down 8.6% in three years and up 6.0% in five. That is 7.9% above the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($742,300).

Apartment homes in Langley: benchmark $522,300, little changed at −0.7% in a month, down 2.2% in three months, down 5.7% in six months, down 8.4% in a year, down 13.6% in three years and little changed at +0.5% in five. That is 13.3% above the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($460,800).

blocks.text: Set against October 2025, Langley had 59 detached sales (79 a year earlier), 76 townhouse sales (71 a year earlier) and 60 apartment sales (75 a year earlier). Month-end active listings were 434 detached (about 495 a year earlier), 260 townhouse (about 316 a year earlier) and 404 apartment (about 555 a year earlier). Dividing sales by active listings gives a sales-to-active ratio of 13.6% for detached, 29.2% for townhouse and 14.9% for apartment.

In dollars, the typical Langley home is worth about $56,400 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $989,300. By type, detached homes lost about $100,700, from $1,548,800 to $1,448,100, townhouses lost about $30,800, from $831,400 to $800,600, and apartments lost about $47,900, from $570,200 to $522,300 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $970,800 six months ago and near $1,041,200 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $37,900 below the six-month mark and about $108,300 below the three-year mark. Against the Fraser Valley Board area, the Langley benchmark is about $72,900 above the regional $860,000; a year earlier the difference was about $70,500 above.
Langley sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 777 Langley houses sold at a median of $1.38M (middle half $1.18M to $1.6M), half of them within 22 days. 768 condos sold at a median of $509,450 (middle half $435,000 to $590,000), half within 27 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.42M to $1.3M between November–January and August–October (149 and 160 sales).

blocks.text: What the Langley figure is
The $932,900 Langley figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Fraser Valley Real Estate Board for October 2026.
